title: Cosmetic ingredient functions
source: European Commission, CosIng 'List of Functions' (official export https://api.tech.ec.europa.eu/cosing20/1.0/api/functions/export-pdf, retrieved 2026-11-15). The `cosing` member is the CosIng function name exactly as published; `definition` is the CosIng description, with obvious typing errors corrected. Commission Decision (EU) 2019/701 is a glossary of common ingredient names only and contains no list of functions. Terms without a `cosing` member are NOT official CosIng functions; their `definition` says so and names the official replacement.

terms.label: Abrasive
terms.definition: Removing unwanted tissue or foreign materials from various body surfaces, including mechanical tooth cleaning and/or gloss improvement.

terms.label: Absorbent
terms.definition: Taking up water- and/or oil-soluble (dissolved or finely dispersed) substances.

terms.label: Adhesive
terms.definition: Tending to unite/bind/bond surfaces together.

terms.label: Anti-seborrheic
terms.definition: Preventing or relieving the symptoms of seborrhea and/or seborrheic dermatitis, including dandruff.

terms.label: Anti-sebum
terms.definition: Helping control sebum production.

terms.label: Anticaking
terms.definition: Preventing agglomeration of particulate solids into lumps or hard masses (cohesive cake), thus allowing free flow of particles.

terms.label: Anticorrosive
terms.definition: Preventing and/or inhibiting the corrosion of the packaging material.

terms.label: Antifoaming
terms.definition: Suppressing foam during manufacturing or reducing the tendency of finished products to generate foam.

terms.label: Antimicrobial
terms.definition: Preventing and/or slowing down microbial growth.

terms.label: Antioxidant
terms.definition: Inhibiting reactions promoted by oxygen, thus avoiding oxidation and rancidity.

terms.label: Antiperspirant
terms.definition: Reducing perspiration.

terms.label: Antiplaque
terms.definition: Helping protect against plaque.

terms.label: Antistatic
terms.definition: Preventing and/or reducing static electricity by neutralising electrical charge on surfaces.

terms.label: Astringent
terms.definition: Contracting and/or tightening the skin.

terms.label: Binding
terms.definition: Providing adhesive properties during and after compression in cosmetic tablets and/or cakes.

terms.label: Bleaching
terms.definition: Bleaching or lightening the shade of hair and/or skin.

terms.label: Buffering
terms.definition: Stabilising the pH of an aqueous medium in a narrow range even if an acid or base is added. Altering and/or maintaining a cosmetic product's pH at the desired level.

terms.label: Bulking
terms.definition: Non-reactive (chemically inert), solid ingredients that dilute other solids and/or increase the volume of cosmetic products.

terms.label: Chelating
terms.definition: Forming complexes with metal ions which could affect the stability and/or appearance of cosmetics.

terms.label: Cleansing
terms.definition: Helping to keep the body surface clean.

terms.label: Colorant
terms.definition: Exclusively or mainly intended to colour the cosmetic product, the body as a whole or certain parts thereof, by absorption or reflection of visible light (precursors of oxidative hair colorants shall be deemed colorants). All authorised colorants are substances in the positive list of Annex IV to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

terms.label: Denaturant
terms.definition: Rendering cosmetics unpalatable. Mostly added to cosmetics containing ethyl alcohol to make it unsuitable for ingestion.

terms.label: Deodorant
terms.definition: Reducing and/or eliminating unpleasant odour. Contributing against the formation of malodour on body surfaces.

terms.label: Depilatory
terms.definition: Breaking down the mechanical strength of hair fibers so that they can be removed by mild scraping/rubbing.

terms.label: Detangling
terms.definition: Reducing or eliminating hair intertwining due to hair surface alteration or damage and, thus, helping combing.

terms.label: Dispersing non-surfactant
terms.definition: Facilitating the dispersion of solids in liquids. They function primarily by coating the solid through the process of adsorption, thus changing the surface characteristic of the suspended solid.

terms.label: Emollient
terms.definition: NON-OFFICIAL: not a current CosIng function. Kept for compatibility because existing dossiers use it. The current CosIng function is SKIN CONDITIONING - EMOLLIENT (key `skin_conditioning_emollient`); prefer that key. EMOLLIENT ('Softens and smooths the skin') was a function in the glossary of Decision 2006/257/EC, which was repealed with effect from 8 May 2020.

terms.label: Emulsifying
terms.definition: NON-OFFICIAL: not a current CosIng function. Kept for compatibility because existing dossiers use it. The current CosIng function is SURFACTANT - EMULSIFYING (key `surfactant_emulsifying`); prefer that key. EMULSIFYING ('Promotes the formation of intimate mixtures of non-miscible liquids by altering the interfacial tension') was a function in the glossary of Decision 2006/257/EC, which was repealed with effect from 8 May 2020.

terms.label: Emulsion stabilising
terms.definition: Helping the process of emulsification and improving emulsion stability and shelf-life.

terms.label: Epilating
terms.definition: Applied to the skin, and stripped off quickly to remove hair. With epilation the entire hair is removed from the follicle, whereas with depilation the hair is removed only to the surface of the skin.

terms.label: Exfoliating
terms.definition: Initiating and/or accelerating removal of the layers of dead skin cells from the skin surface.

terms.label: Eyelash conditioning
terms.definition: Conditioning and enhancing the appearance of eyelashes. Improving the gloss or sheen of eyelashes, coating the eyelash hair to increase the appearance of its diameter and length, or helping with the separation of the eyelash hair.

terms.label: Film forming
terms.definition: Producing (upon application) a continuous film on the skin, hair or nails.

terms.label: Flavouring
terms.definition: Imparting taste and/or flavour to a cosmetic product.

terms.label: Foaming
terms.definition: Trapping numerous small bubbles of air or other gas within a small volume of liquid by modifying the surface tension of the liquid.

terms.label: Fragrance
terms.definition: Imparting an odour or taste. Creating a perceivable pleasant smell and/or masking a bad smell.

terms.label: Gel forming
terms.definition: Giving the consistency of a gel (a semi-solid preparation with some elasticity) to a liquid preparation.

terms.label: Hair conditioning
terms.definition: Enhancing the appearance and feel of hair. Leaving the hair easy to comb, supple, soft and shiny and/or imparting volume, lightness, gloss, texture, etc.

terms.label: Hair dyeing
terms.definition: Imparting color to hair. Hair dyeing preparations may be temporary, semi-permanent, permanent, depending on the length of time the colorant remains on the hair.

terms.label: Hair fixing
terms.definition: Permitting physical control of hair style.

terms.label: Hair waving or straightening
terms.definition: Modifying the chemical structure of the hair, allowing it to be set in the style required (permanent waves or hair straightening).

terms.label: Humectant
terms.definition: Retaining and/or preserving the moisture in a product during use.

terms.label: Keratolytic
terms.definition: Helping to eliminate the dead cells of the stratum corneum.

terms.label: Light stabilizer
terms.definition: Protecting the cosmetic product from deterioration effects of light.

terms.label: Lytic
terms.definition: Helping to break down lipids, proteins, and polysaccharides into smaller components, usually by the action of enzymes.

terms.label: Moisturising
terms.definition: Increasing the water content of the skin and keeping it soft and smooth.

terms.label: Nail conditioning
terms.definition: Improving and/or enhancing the cosmetic characteristics of the nail (moisturizing, increasing sheen, reducing brittleness and flaking, etc.).

terms.label: Nail sculpting
terms.definition: Forming a hard structure that resembles the nail plate.

terms.label: Not reported
terms.definition: No function currently reported.

terms.label: Occlusive
terms.definition: Preventing and/or slowing down the evaporation of water from the skin surface.

terms.label: Opacifying
terms.definition: Reducing transparency or translucency of cosmetics.

terms.label: Oral care
terms.definition: Providing cosmetic effects to the oral cavity, e.g. cleansing, deodorising, protecting.

terms.label: Oxidising
terms.definition: Changing the chemical nature of another ingredient by adding oxygen (or removing hydrogen).

terms.label: Pearlescent
terms.definition: Imparting a nacreous appearance to cosmetics.

terms.label: Perfuming
terms.definition: Used for perfume and aromatic raw materials.

terms.label: pH adjusters
terms.definition: Controlling the pH of cosmetic products.

terms.label: Plasticiser
terms.definition: Softening and making supple synthetic polymers that otherwise could not be easily deformed, spread or worked out.

terms.label: Preservative
terms.definition: Exclusively or mainly intended to inhibit the development of micro-organisms in the cosmetic product. All authorised preservatives are substances in the positive list of Annex V to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

terms.label: Propellant
terms.definition: Generating pressure in an aerosol pack, expelling contents when the valve is opened. Some liquefied propellants can act as solvents.

terms.label: Reducing
terms.definition: Changing the chemical nature of another ingredient by adding hydrogen (or removing oxygen).

terms.label: Refatting
terms.definition: Replenishing the lipids of the hair or of the top layers of the skin.

terms.label: Refreshing
terms.definition: Imparting a pleasant freshness to the skin.

terms.label: Skin conditioning
terms.definition: Maintaining the skin in good condition.

terms.label: Skin conditioning - emollient
terms.definition: Acting as lubricants on the skin surface providing the skin with a soft and smooth appearance.

terms.label: Skin conditioning - humectant
terms.definition: Increasing the water content of the top layers of the skin. Humectants are primarily hygroscopic agents drawing moisture from the surrounding air.

terms.label: Skin conditioning - miscellaneous
terms.definition: Enhancing the appearance of dry and/or damaged skin by reducing flaking and restoring suppleness.

terms.label: Skin conditioning - occlusive
terms.definition: Retarding the evaporation of water from the skin surface. Occlusives are generally lipids which tend to remain on the skin surface and thus increase the water content of skin.

terms.label: Skin protecting
terms.definition: Helping to avoid harmful effects to the skin from external factors.

terms.label: Slip modifier
terms.definition: Enhancing the flow properties of other ingredients without reacting chemically with them.

terms.label: Smoothing
terms.definition: Seeking to achieve an even skin surface by decreasing roughness or irregularities.

terms.label: Solvent
terms.definition: Dissolving other components of cosmetics. Solvents are usually liquids (aqueous and nonaqueous).

terms.label: Soothing
terms.definition: Lightening discomfort of the skin or of the scalp.

terms.label: Surface modifier
terms.definition: Applied to other cosmetic components to make them more hydrophilic or hydrophobic, or to modify their physical/chemical properties (in some cases, surface modifiers may form a covalent bond with substrates).

terms.label: Surfactant
terms.definition: Helping other ingredients that normally do not mix to dissolve or disperse in one another. Surfactants are also called surface active agents as they lower the surface tension of water or reduce the interfacial tension between immiscible components.

terms.label: Surfactant - cleansing
terms.definition: Wetting body surfaces, emulsifying or solubilizing oils, and suspending soil (generally, such ingredients contribute to the foaming and lathering properties of cleansing products).

terms.label: Surfactant - dispersing
terms.definition: Helping distribute an insoluble solid in a liquid phase.

terms.label: Surfactant - emulsifying
terms.definition: Helping suspensions or dispersions of liquids in a second liquid by reducing the surface tension of the substances to be emulsified.

terms.label: Surfactant - foam boosting
terms.definition: Increasing foaming capacity and/or stabilizing foams in general.

terms.label: Surfactant - hydrotrope
terms.definition: Enhancing the water solubility of another surfactant.

terms.label: Surfactant - solubilizing
terms.definition: Helping another component (solute) to dissolve in a medium in which it is not normally soluble.

terms.label: Tanning
terms.definition: Darkening the skin with or without exposure to UV.

terms.label: Tonic
terms.definition: Producing a feeling of well-being on skin and hair.

terms.label: UV absorber
terms.definition: Protecting the cosmetic product from the effects of UV-light.

terms.label: UV filter
terms.definition: Exclusively or mainly intended to protect the skin and/or hair against certain UV radiation by absorbing, reflecting or scattering UV radiation. All authorised UV filters are substances in the positive list of Annex VI to the Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

terms.label: Viscosity controlling
terms.definition: Increasing or decreasing the viscosity (thickness) of cosmetics.
